name: ExpertPrompting
executive_summary: Automatically synthesize a detailed, instruction-specific expert-identity description, then condition the answer on that generated persona — an automated, per-instruction version of hand-writing a persona into a prompt.
description: Rather than a single fixed persona ('You are an expert...') applied uniformly, ExpertPrompting generates a customized expert identity tailored to each specific instruction — distinguished, informative, and automatic by design — using a small number of hand-revised identity exemplars as in-context guidance for the generation step. The augmented instructions (identity + original instruction) were used to produce a new instruction-following dataset with GPT-3.5, training an open-source assistant (ExpertLLaMA) that reportedly reaches 96% of ChatGPT's capability by GPT4-based evaluation, with expert-conditioned answers preferred over vanilla answers 48.5% to 23% by a reviewer model.
when_to_use: Instructions where framing the answer as coming from a specific, well-matched expert persona would plausibly improve depth or relevance, and hand-writing a persona per instruction isn't practical at scale.
when_not_to_use: Simple factual or formatting tasks where an expert framing adds no value.
Domains where a fabricated persona (implying credentials the assistant doesn't have) is undesirable or could mislead the user about its actual capabilities.
known_pitfalls: The synthesized expert identity is itself a generated artifact and can be generic or mismatched if the in-context exemplars don't cover the instruction's domain well.

primary_source.authors: Xu, Yang, Lin, Wang, Zhou, Zhang, Mao
primary_source.title: ExpertPrompting: Instructing Large Language Models to be Distinguished Experts
